uncited: A method using an Invertible Neural Network (INN) to transform view space points to canonical space and learn skinning weights simultaneously, replacing iterative root-finding methods like Broyden's to speed up training.

It transforms deformed space points $x_v$ to an initial canonical approximation $x_{\text{init}_c}$ using the nearest joint's one-hot vector $w'$ and posed skeleton $B_i$: $x_{\text{init}_c} = (\sum_{i=1}^{nb} w'_i \cdot B_i)^{-1} \cdot x_v$.

It predicts skinning weight $w_s$ at canonical space from predicted canonical points $x'_c$ using network $G_{x_c \to w}^W$, then calculates final canonical points $x_c = (\sum_{i=1}^{nb} w_{s,i} \cdot B_i) \cdot x_v$.
The INN $G_{v \to c}^{\text{INN}}$ is conditioned on per-frame 3D skeleton $J$, mapping view space to canonical space.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot J)$ per Gaussian per frame, where $N$ is the number of Gaussians and $J$ is the number of joints.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot J)$ to store skinning weights.
*   **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.
Linear Blend Skinning for Gaussian Splatting was introduced in the context of human avatar modeling using 3D Gaussian Splatting.
It builds on the SMPL body model and adapts LBS to work with canonical Gaussians.
